case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Farid Khan and Others
facts: These appeals are preferred by the State of Uttar Pradesh assailing the acquittal of the three respondents accused of the offences charged against them u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC.
The incident giving rise to the present appeals happened on 2.8.1978 at about 5.45 P.M. in Mohalla Mazar Tat.

On the date of occurrence, Achhey Mian, brother of deceased Khurshid Mian, who lived in Mohalla Nalapar, visited his brother Khurshid Mian to discuss about the arrangements for the Chaalisvan [the fortieth day ceremony] of their late father.
The accused persons surrounded Khurshid Mian and immediately started attacking him with knives.
The deceased fell on the ground and died on the spot.
Investigation of the case was taken over by PW-6, who prepared the inquest report.
Post-mortem examination on the dead body of the deceased was conducted by PW-4.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and they alleged false implication.
On the side of the prosecution, six witnesses were examined.
issues: Whether the evidence of the three eye-witnesses proves that the respondents are guilty of the offence of murder punishable u/s. 302 read with Section 34 IPC?
petitioner_arguments: The State of Uttar Pradesh argued that the Sessions Court rightly placed reliance on the evidence of the three eye-witnesses and that the High Court erred in disbelieving their testimony.
respondent_arguments: The respondents argued that the witnesses spoke falsehood and that they had not seen any incident.
They alleged that Achhey Mian, in collusion with the police, implicated the accused as he was inimically disposed towards them.
court_reasoning: The court held that the evidence of the three eye-witnesses proves that A-1 Saghir s/o Zakkan Khan stabbed on the chest of the deceased whereas A-2 Amir Ahmad and A-3 Farid Khan caused injuries on the back and legs of the deceased.
The court rejected the High Court's reasoning that witness Achhey Mian could not have been present at the place of incident on the date of the occurrence.
holding: The final decision is that the acquittal of the three respondents accused of the offences charged against them u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC is set aside and they are found guilty of the offence of murder punishable u/s. 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
cases_cited: State of Uttar Pradesh v Farid Khan
